sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A small clumping cactus of dry grasslands and rocky openings in the central United States. Escobaria missouriensis is an older name; Kew currently treats the species as Pelecyphora missouriensis.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: The 5–8 cm spherical stems form clumps that may reach about 30 cm tall and wide. Spring flowers are greenish to bronze; the fruits become reddish.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: No reliable food use is established by the sources consulted.
